asx200.note: Approximate; the ASX 200 sits near 8,811 after easing 0.38% on 6 July, having gained modestly through a volatile FY26.

sp500.note: Approximate; the S&P 500 traded around 7,483 in early July 2026, near record territory alongside a record Dow.

nasdaq.note: Approximate; the Nasdaq Composite was around 25,833 in early July 2026 but wobbled as some chip names pulled back.

marketSnapshot.commentary: The environment is unusual: the RBA has raised the cash rate three times in 2026 to 4.35% as an oil-supply shock keeps Australian inflation sticky, while the US Fed holds at 3.50-3.75% with a mild hike bias. US equities are near records led by AI and mega-cap tech, and the ASX has lagged, buoyed mainly by a strong iron-ore-driven BHP but dragged by a sharp CSL de-rating. The AUD near 0.69 lifts unhedged US-dollar returns for Australian investors. Key risks are renewed energy-price and inflation surprises, higher-for-longer rates pressuring rate-sensitive assets, and stretched valuations in AI/semiconductors.

sectors.name: AI & semiconductors
sectors.note: Structural AI capex remains the dominant global growth theme, with TSMC guiding 2026 revenue up more than 30%, though valuations are elevated and prone to sharp pullbacks.

sectors.name: Data centres / digital infrastructure
sectors.note: Surging compute and cloud demand underpins strong leasing; Australian names like NextDC and Goodman continue to expand capacity, but funding and power constraints are watch points.

sectors.name: Healthcare
sectors.note: Sentiment is weak after CSL's guidance cuts, ~US$5bn impairments and a slipping Seqirus demerger, though depressed valuations may offer selective long-term value.

sectors.name: Australian banks / financials
sectors.note: Higher-for-longer rates support net interest margins, but stretched valuations (CBA) and slowing credit growth temper upside; diversified earners like Macquarie look better balanced.

sectors.name: Resources / materials
sectors.note: Iron ore strength drove BHP up more than 60% in FY26 on resilient Chinese demand, though the sector remains highly cyclical and China-dependent.

sectors.name: Listed infrastructure / utilities
sectors.note: Toll roads and pipelines offer inflation-linked, defensive cash flows and 4.7-6.3% yields, but rising bond yields under RBA hikes cap capital upside.

sectors.name: Energy transition
sectors.note: Grid, gas-firming and renewables build-out remains a multi-decade tailwind for owners like APA, but higher capital costs and policy uncertainty weigh on near-term returns.

companies.name: Commonwealth Bank of Australia
companies.thesis: Australia's largest bank benefits from higher-for-longer rates supporting margins and a dominant, low-risk mortgage franchise with strong capital returns. Its scale, deposit base and technology lead sustain sector-leading returns on equity.
companies.risks: Premium valuation near the top of its historical range and slowing credit growth leave little margin for disappointment.
companies.recent: Shares rebounded to about A$165 in early July 2026, mid-way in a 52-week range of roughly A$150-186.

companies.name: CSL Limited
companies.thesis: A global plasma and biotech leader whose core Behring franchise retains durable demand and pricing power. After a ~50% de-rating the valuation is far more modest, offering recovery potential if margins and the Seqirus separation stabilise.
companies.risks: Cut FY26 guidance, ~US$5bn Vifor impairments, weak flu-vaccine outlook and a slipping Seqirus demerger keep execution risk high.
companies.recent: Shares hit decade lows near A$92 in June 2026 before recovering toward A$116, down sharply year-to-date.

companies.name: BHP Group
companies.thesis: The world's largest miner is riding resilient iron-ore prices and strong Chinese demand, complemented by growing copper exposure geared to electrification. Low-cost Pilbara operations generate substantial free cash flow and dividends.
companies.risks: Heavy dependence on Chinese steel demand and iron-ore prices makes earnings highly cyclical.
companies.recent: Shares climbed more than 60% in FY26 to around A$60.54, vastly outperforming the ASX 200.

companies.name: Wesfarmers
companies.thesis: A diversified conglomerate anchored by the highly profitable Bunnings and Kmart retail businesses, with optionality in chemicals, health and lithium. Strong cash generation and disciplined capital allocation support consistent returns.
companies.risks: A rich earnings multiple and consumer-spending sensitivity to high rates limit near-term upside.
companies.recent: Shares traded around A$88 in early July 2026, up from a prior close near A$87.

companies.name: Macquarie Group
companies.thesis: A globally diversified financial with leading positions in infrastructure asset management, commodities trading and green-energy investment. Annuity-style asset-management earnings plus markets upside give it a differentiated, less rate-dependent profile.
companies.risks: Market-facing income is volatile and deal-flow dependent, and asset realisations can be lumpy.
companies.recent: Shares traded around A$250 in late June/early July 2026.

companies.name: Goodman Group
companies.thesis: A global industrial-property and logistics landlord pivoting aggressively into data-centre development to capture AI and cloud demand. A premium land bank in supply-constrained markets and a large development pipeline support growth in earnings and assets under management.
companies.risks: Development execution, power availability and higher funding costs from elevated rates are key risks.
companies.recent: Units traded around A$30.78 in early July 2026 after pulling back from prior highs.

companies.name: NextDC
companies.thesis: Australia's leading independent data-centre operator is expanding capacity to meet booming AI and cloud demand, with strong contracted forward order books. Scarcity of hyperscale-ready sites and power gives it a durable competitive moat.
companies.risks: Heavy capital expenditure, ongoing losses and reliance on continued funding make it sensitive to rates and execution.
companies.recent: Shares traded around A$14.78 in early July 2026, up about 18% year-to-date.

companies.name: Transurban Group
companies.thesis: The dominant owner of Australian toll roads offers inflation-linked, largely defensive traffic-based cash flows across Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane networks. Contracted CPI-linked toll escalators provide a partial inflation hedge and steady distributions.
companies.risks: High leverage and long-duration cash flows make the units sensitive to rising bond yields under RBA tightening.
companies.recent: Units traded around A$14.48 in early July 2026 with a distribution yield near 4.7%.

companies.name: APA Group
companies.thesis: Australia's largest energy-infrastructure owner transports more than half the nation's gas and is investing in electricity, solar and wind assets tied to the energy transition. Regulated and contracted revenues support a high, growing distribution yielding above 6%.
companies.risks: High gearing exposes it to rising rates, and the long-run gas outlook and regulatory settings add uncertainty.
companies.recent: Units traded around A$9.95 in early July 2026, yielding roughly 6.3%.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.thesis: The dominant supplier of AI accelerators and the CUDA software ecosystem remains at the centre of global AI infrastructure spending. Hyperscaler and sovereign-AI demand continues to drive rapid revenue and earnings growth.
companies.risks: Very high expectations, customer concentration and potential AI-capex digestion make the stock volatile.
companies.recent: Shares traded near US$197 in early July 2026, easing modestly as some chip names pulled back.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.thesis: A diversified software and cloud leader monetising AI across Azure, Copilot and its enterprise franchise. Recurring subscription revenue and a strong balance sheet underpin durable, compounding growth.
companies.risks: Heavy AI-related capital spending and a full valuation could pressure returns if cloud growth slows.
companies.recent: Shares traded around US$390 in early July 2026.

companies.name: Apple
companies.thesis: A globally entrenched hardware-and-services ecosystem with an enormous, loyal installed base and growing high-margin services revenue. Strong cash generation funds large buybacks and steady capital returns.
companies.risks: Slower device upgrade cycles, China exposure and a lagging AI narrative are key concerns.
companies.recent: Shares traded around US$305 in early July 2026 after touching a 52-week high near US$317 in June.

companies.name: Alphabet
companies.thesis: A dominant search and digital-advertising franchise with fast-growing Google Cloud and leading AI research through DeepMind and Gemini. Strong free cash flow and a broadening AI product suite support the growth outlook.
companies.risks: AI disruption to search, heavy cloud capex and ongoing antitrust scrutiny are notable risks.
companies.recent: Shares traded around US$359 in early July 2026, with a market cap near US$4.4 trillion.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.thesis: A leader in e-commerce and cloud, with AWS a primary beneficiary of AI workloads and improving retail margins. Expanding advertising and logistics efficiency add multiple profit drivers.
companies.risks: Elevated capital spending, competitive cloud dynamics and consumer-demand sensitivity are key risks.
companies.recent: Shares traded around US$243 in early July 2026.

companies.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing
companies.thesis: The world's leading advanced-chip foundry manufactures the processors powering AI, with unmatched leading-edge process technology. Management guided 2026 revenue up more than 30% on structural AI demand.
companies.risks: Geopolitical risk around Taiwan and cyclicality in non-AI semiconductor end-markets are the main concerns.
companies.recent: ADRs traded around US$434 in early July 2026 ahead of Q2 results due 19 July; Q1 revenue rose 35% year-on-year.

suggestions.title: Stay diversified across regions as the US and Australia diverge
suggestions.rationale: The Fed is on hold near 3.75% while the RBA is still hiking to 4.35% on an oil-driven inflation shock, creating diverging equity and currency dynamics. Broad global and domestic exposure spreads this policy and single-market risk. Regular contributions (as in a Spaceship-style plan) smooth entry points.

suggestions.title: Mind currency: a ~0.69 AUD lifts unhedged US returns
suggestions.rationale: With the AUD near 0.69, unhedged global funds have benefited from a weaker local dollar, but that tailwind can reverse if the AUD rallies. Blending hedged and unhedged exposure reduces reliance on any single currency outcome. This is a portfolio-construction consideration, not a currency call.

suggestions.title: Treat the AI/semiconductor theme as high-conviction but high-volatility
suggestions.rationale: AI leaders like NVIDIA, TSMC, Microsoft and Alphabet are driving global index gains, with TSMC guiding 2026 revenue up over 30%. Valuations are elevated and prone to sharp drawdowns, as early-July chip weakness showed. Sizing positions modestly and holding for the long term suits this theme better than chasing momentum.

suggestions.title: Digital-infrastructure exposure as an AI derivative
suggestions.rationale: Data-centre owners such as NextDC and Goodman Group capture AI and cloud demand through physical capacity rather than chip cycles. Scarcity of power and hyperscale-ready sites supports pricing, though heavy capex and rate sensitivity are risks. It offers a differentiated way to participate in the AI build-out.

suggestions.title: Use listed infrastructure and utilities for defensive, inflation-linked income
suggestions.rationale: Toll roads (Transurban) and pipelines (APA) offer CPI-linked cash flows and yields of roughly 4.7-6.3% that can partly offset sticky inflation. Rising bond yields under RBA hikes cap capital upside, so these suit income and diversification rather than growth. Leverage levels are worth monitoring.

suggestions.title: Recognise concentration risk in the big Australian banks
suggestions.rationale: CBA and peers trade on premium multiples and dominate the ASX 200, so a bank-heavy portfolio carries hidden concentration. Higher-for-longer rates support margins, but slowing credit growth limits upside. Balancing financials with resources and global exposure reduces single-sector dependence.

suggestions.title: Resources offer cyclical upside but demand China awareness
suggestions.rationale: BHP surged more than 60% in FY26 on resilient iron-ore prices and Chinese demand, illustrating the sector's leverage. Those same drivers make earnings and share prices highly cyclical and China-dependent. Position sizing should reflect that commodity volatility.

suggestions.title: Consider CSL only as a contrarian, patient position
suggestions.rationale: CSL has de-rated roughly 50% on guidance cuts, ~US$5bn impairments and a delayed Seqirus demerger, leaving a beaten-down valuation. The core plasma franchise remains globally strong, offering recovery potential if execution stabilises. This is a higher-risk turnaround idea, not a defensive holding.

suggestions.title: Keep cash and defensives given elevated Australian rates
suggestions.rationale: With the RBA cash rate at 4.35% and inflation still sticky, cash and term deposits offer competitive risk-free returns. Holding some dry powder provides flexibility to invest into any volatility. This balances an equity-heavy long-term plan.

suggestions.title: Prefer quality compounders over speculative names
suggestions.rationale: Diversified, cash-generative businesses such as Macquarie, Wesfarmers, Microsoft and Alphabet combine multiple earnings drivers with strong balance sheets. In a higher-rate, valuation-sensitive market, durable free cash flow tends to be rewarded. Focusing on quality reduces reliance on any single theme.

suggestions.title: Rebalance periodically after wide dispersion in 2026
suggestions.rationale: Sharp divergence between winners (BHP, AI mega-caps) and losers (CSL) has likely skewed portfolio weightings. Periodic rebalancing trims outsized positions and restores intended diversification. It is a discipline that manages risk rather than a market-timing call.
